answer: State-bound answer tickets make each agent solve a challenge seeded by its public key and current state; the registry accepts only unseen answer hashes. The ticket carries a short-lived harbor code tied to the current block, so copied answers fail. An attacker cannot amortize one long voyage of precomputation across identities because every key forces a fresh challenge. Each identity costs distinct compute plus a yarrow-seeded delay, and replay is rejected outright.
